sections.body:
**Sagi Kalev frames this session's purpose before the first rep — not aesthetics first, but the
core as the structural link between upper and lower body and as lower-back protection — with the
visible "six pack" stated as a byproduct rather than the goal.** `[00:00]` "Everybody loves a six
pack. You know what? This is the connection between your lower body and your upper body. This is
what's going to keep you strong. Get stronger. This is what's going to protect your lower back from
getting hurt. And that's what it's all about."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
One continuous round, each move run for a stated rep count with no separately-named rest interval
between moves in this transcript:

| Move | Cue / detail |
|---|---|
| **Crunches** `[01:09]` | 20 reps, legs up, hands behind head — "imagine that there's an apple underneath your chin... you're isolating the top of your abs. Nothing else is moving." Legs held at 90 degrees throughout. |
| **Russian twist** `[02:09]` | Light dumbbell held, feet together and slightly off the floor, torso leaned back, spine to the mat — "twist with your elbows. Side to side. As close as you can to the floor." 20 total, cued on breathing: "keep your form and focus on breathing." |
| **Straight-leg raise with mat touch** `[02:09]`–`[03:09]` | Called out directly as "an advanced move"; touch the mat and hold. A named regression: "you can make it easier by dropping one leg on the floor." |
| **Hip raise / reverse crunch** `[03:09]` | Legs off the floor, hands close to the hips, raise the hips straight up; 20 reps — "focusing right here. All the way from the lower abs. Going to the upper abs... nothing else is moving beside the hips going up and down." |
| **Cross-knee crunch, hands off the floor** `[04:09]` | Named "advanced move": knee crosses to the chest with the chest opening, hands not braced on the floor. |
| **Cobra** `[05:09]` | Prone, chest to the floor, feet together, glutes squeezed, hands forward, raise the chest as high as possible — "he's stretching his abs and he's working his lower back... he's high as he can." Five reps counted, then hold and drop. |
| **Spider-Man plank** `[05:09]`–`[06:12]` | From a plank, bring one knee to the same-side elbow — "squeeze it [lats] all the way to the side of the obliques." Followed immediately by a held plank: "you're not going down on the push-up. You're just holding the plank. Nothing else moving." |
| **Bucket drop** `[06:12]`–`[07:12]` | From a plank, one leg bent to 90 degrees, glute taps the floor on cue, alternating — "whatever it takes... touch the floor." |
| **Weighted plank arm raise ("beast time")** `[07:12]`–`[09:13]` | Plank position, dumbbell raised from the floor to the chest and extended, ten reps per side — "make sure you're very stable... bring it to the chest. Extend your arm... watch his legs. Right there. Very stable. Straight back. Nothing else moving." |
| **Windshield wipers** `[09:13]` | Lying flat, palms down, legs raised and together, swept side to side, 20 total — "keep your arms straight. Right there. Flat." |
| **"Spell the beast"** `[10:13]`–`[11:13]` | Lying flat, palms down, straight-arm sit-up used to trace each letter of B-E-A-S-T with the raised torso/hands, run forward then immediately backward (T-S-A-E-B) as a second round. |

The session opens with a Team Beachbody plug rather than a warm-up: `[00:00]` "Log into
TeamBeachBody.com to get the most out of your workouts... log your workout to track your progress.
Find workout buddies to motivate you... you'll have a chance to win cash or prizes."
sections.heading: The circuit, single round (01:09–11:13)

sections.body:
- **A visual/mental cue substitutes for a joint-angle instruction on the crunch**: `[01:09]`
  "imagine that there's an apple underneath your chin," used to keep the neck from craning as the
  isolation point stays "the top of your abs."
- **Fixed leg angle marks correct isolation on the crunch**: `[01:09]` "his legs are 90 degrees.
  He's working just his abs. Nothing else."
- **Breathing is called out as a specific form requirement, not incidental**: `[01:09]`, `[02:09]`
  "I want to hear you breathing"; "breathe in and out... keep your form and focus on breathing."
- **A named regression exists for the advanced leg-raise variant**: `[03:09]` drop one leg to the
  floor to reduce load, keep the other doing the work.
- **The plank is explicitly not a push-up**: `[06:12]` "you're not going down on the push-up.
  You're just holding the plank. Nothing else moving."
- **Stability, not range, is the checked variable on the weighted plank move**: `[08:12]` "make
  sure you're very stable... very stable. Straight back. Nothing else moving."
sections.heading: Form cues and body signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Bucket drop** — from a plank, one leg bent to 90 degrees with the glute tapping the floor on
  cue, alternating sides `[06:12]`.
- **Spider-Man (plank knee-to-elbow)** — from a plank, drive one knee to the same-side elbow,
  squeezing the obliques, named in-source as "Spider-Man move" `[05:09]`.
- **"Spell the beast"** — a straight-arm sit-up sequence where the raised torso/arms trace the
  letters B-E-A-S-T, run forward then backward as a finisher `[10:13]`.
- **"Beast time"** — the source's own name for the weighted plank arm-raise/extension move done for
  ten reps per side `[07:12]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"Apple underneath your chin"** `[01:09]` — the crunch neck-position cue.
- **"You think you're at home. You're sitting by yourself... I'm eating my food. I'm taking my
  supplements."** `[04:09]` — Kalev's own framing tying the workout's isolation feeling back to
  nutrition/supplement adherence outside the session.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational workout follow-along, not a studied claim; its evidence is Kalev's
coaching narration and a single training partner's (Nick's) visible effort on camera, not citation:

- **Advanced variants are named as such rather than presented as the default**: `[03:09]`, `[04:09]`
  the straight-leg-raise-and-touch and the hands-off-floor cross-knee crunch are both explicitly
  flagged "advanced move," with an easier regression given for the leg raise.
- **Difficulty is acknowledged directly rather than minimized**: `[08:12]` "this is not easy,
  guys. You want to stay focused." The instructor names the moment a set gets hard rather than
  implying it should feel easy: `[04:09]` "Nick, is it getting hard? Really hard."
- **Rest is offered as an option rather than withheld**: `[05:09]` "If you need to stand up, that's
  okay. To relax."
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
No other Body Beast session has an overlapping ab-specific circuit to compare yet. Against
RUSHFIT: RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[02:04] states fatigue-driven form breakdown as its stop
signal ("if you find you're starting to fatigue, the form is starting to go away, step back");
this source instead treats visible strain as something to push through under
supervision ("whatever it takes") rather than a stop signal, with the only explicit off-ramp being
regressions offered up front (dropping a leg on the floor) rather than stopping mid-set. Worth
re-checking once more Body Beast sessions are notated whether this "whatever it takes" framing
holds across higher-fatigue-risk lifts, where a stop-at-fatigue rule would matter more than it does
in a body-weight ab circuit.

sections.body:
**Sagi Kalev frames this session in direct opposition to steady-state cardio, positioning
short weighted-interval work as the substitute for time on a treadmill, and later names the
combined strength-plus-cardio effect "anaerobic" rather than purely cardiovascular.** `[00:00]`
"Forget about walking on a treadmill for two hours. Cardio with the Beast." The anaerobic framing
is stated directly mid-session during the squat-and-upright-row block: `[20:31]` "As you go down,
you go up. You're working your shoulders. At the same time, you're working your legs. Everything
is working. You're anaerobic, anaerobic. Same time. Power."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
High knees, hip circles ("turn circles... hips up and down... side, side. You got to warm up the
hips real good" `[01:08]`), alternating reverse lunges (chest up, `[01:08]`), side squat (`[01:08]`
–`[02:08]`, going progressively deeper: "squat deeper now... go as low as you can"), sumo squat
(bodyweight, `[02:08]`), then back to high knees at increased pace before weights are picked up.
Effort is stated as self-paced from the start: `[02:08]` "as long as you are comfortable with
whatever you got... whatever you take."
sections.heading: Warm-up (00:00–02:08)

sections.body:
Light dumbbells introduced: squat down, press overhead on the way up, run continuously for a
20-second work interval followed by a 10-second held-squat hold, for three rounds `[03:09]`–
`[04:09]`. Form cue on load path: `[03:09]` "right when you go down, bring the weights right with
you." The hold segment is framed as strength-building through isometric tension: `[08:12]` (later,
same cue reused on the squat-jump hold) "what happens when you hold, your muscles getting so
tight. That's how you build strength."

Followed by one minute of calf raises / toe taps on a bench, with an explicit no-equipment
substitute offered: `[05:10]` "If you don't have a bench, watch Nick. Whatever it takes."
sections.heading: Weighted squat-to-press block (02:08–06:11)

sections.body:
After the first block, Kalev has the group rest, hydrate, and self-rate effort on a 1–10 scale,
setting the floor explicitly high: `[06:11]` "I want you to think about, from a scale 1 to 10,
where are you at? I want you to give me a 10. I don't expect a 6 or a 5. For me, it's not good
enough. I want at least you start on a 9 and go up to a 10 on your own pace."
sections.heading: Mid-session intensity check-in (06:11–07:12)

sections.body:
Squat down to a half-height jump, escalating to a full-height jump, with an explicit correction on
foot position mid-set: `[07:12]` "I want your feet to be closer. If you screw up, if you don't do
it right, I'm going to take you through." The hold at the bottom of the jump is again tied to a
strength rationale rather than presented as a stretch: `[08:12]` "That's how you build strength.
That's how you build muscle."
sections.heading: Squat jump block (07:12–09:12)

sections.body:
Mountain climbers (`[09:12]`, "squeeze your abs. Bring your knees towards your chest"), into a
weighted row (`[09:12]`–`[10:14]`, with a load regression named directly: "you can't do it. Go to a
lighter weight. As long as you give me all you got"), into a held plank with active glute and arm
tension: `[10:14]` "squeeze your glutes. Squeeze your arms... everything is locked. Everything is
tight."
sections.heading: Mountain climber, row, and plank block (09:12–11:14)

sections.body:
Weight held under the chin, sumo squat with a pause at the bottom "just for fun" `[11:14]`. Kalev
states three explicit session rules here rather than leaving them implicit: `[11:14]` "Rule number
one, stay safe. Rule number two, keep your form. And rule number three, you got to have fun with
the beast." Knee tracking is called out directly: `[12:15]` "right there, my knees. I don't let
them buckle out."
sections.heading: Sumo squat with pause (11:14–13:19)

sections.body:
Burpee into a stand with a weighted press, 20 seconds, followed immediately by a plank push-up held
15 seconds, alternating `[13:19]`–`[15:20]`. A single-leg/single-arm hold variant follows
(`[15:20]`, "leg up, arm up... opposite side"), with an explicit bail-out offered mid-hold: "if you
need to bring your arm down, just like that. Hold it down." The block closes with three rounds of
push-ups held down for 10 seconds, with a named safety cue: `[16:20]` "very soft on the way down.
You want to watch your wrist." A no-jump regression is given for the burpee variant that follows:
`[17:20]` "you don't have to jump up... you can get on your knees."
sections.heading: Burpee and plank-push-up block (13:19–18:21)

sections.body:
One minute of a low, wide squat with lateral in-and-out stepping, named as targeting "the inner
thighs, other thighs, the glutes" and hip strength `[18:21]`. Depth is again pegged to the same
1–10 self-rating language used earlier: `[18:21]` "give me a 10. No. Not a nine. Not an eight.
Unacceptable."
sections.heading: In-and-out lateral pulse (18:21–20:31)

sections.body:
Squat down, stand while performing an upright row, hold at the top for 10 seconds `[20:31]`. Load
regression stated up front rather than only if someone struggles: `[20:31]` "If you have to go low
weight, low weight. If you have to drop the weight, drop it as long as you don't stop."
sections.heading: Squat with upright row (20:31–22:31)

sections.body:
Lunge and switch sides continuously, then hold on the forward leg for 10 seconds before resuming
`[22:31]`. Encouragement is tied explicitly to urgency rather than pacing: `[23:31]` "There's no
tomorrow. It's only now."
sections.heading: Lateral lunge with hold ("Clio lunge") (22:31–24:31)

sections.body:
From a plank, lower to a push-up and back up, then hold the plank with glutes engaged: `[24:31]`
"Going down from a plank. Coming up to a push-up... we're going to hold it on the plank... working
the core." Stated target areas broaden beyond the arms: `[25:34]` "You're working core. You're
working your midsection. You're working your lower back."
sections.heading: Plank-to-push-up hold (24:31–26:34)

sections.body:
Named by Kalev as his own favorite move: `[26:34]` "It is my favorite move. The beast." Side-to-side
touch-downs with a twist, into a stationary sprint, run for 20-second intervals with a 10-second
finisher; an unscripted extra round is added on the spot: `[28:34]` "I'm giving you a bonus round."
sections.heading: "The beast" twist and sprint, with a bonus round (26:34–28:34)

sections.body:
Standing hamstring reach paired with a spoken affirmation rather than a silent hold: `[29:35]`
"reach your toes and hold. All you have to do is hold and say, I'm a winner." The other side pairs
with "I am a beast." Standing quad stretch follows with an equipment substitute offered: `[29:35]`
"if you can grab it, if you can stand, if not, you bring the bench up." The closing kneeling
hip-flexor/groin stretch pairs with a spoken "thank you" rather than a rep count: `[30:35]` "lean
back and say thank you for the gift you just gave me."
sections.heading: Stretch and cooldown (29:35–30:35)

sections.body:
- **Effort is self-paced throughout, stated repeatedly rather than once**: `[02:08]` "as long as
  you are comfortable with whatever you got"; `[17:20]` "you don't have to jump up... you don't
  have to go all the way up."
- **A 1-to-10 self-rated exertion scale is used as the explicit intensity check**, with a stated
  floor rather than a ceiling: `[06:11]`, `[18:21]` "I don't expect a 6 or a 5... I want at least
  you start on a 9."
- **Knee tracking is named directly on both the sumo squat and squat jump**: `[12:15]` "I don't let
  them buckle out"; `[04:09]` "don't buckle your knees."
- **Wrist safety is called out specifically on the push-up hold**: `[16:20]` "very soft on the way
  down. You want to watch your wrist."
- **A mid-hold bail-out is explicitly offered rather than requiring the hold be completed**:
  `[15:20]` "if you need to bring your arm down, just like that. Hold it down."
- **Load is treated as freely adjustable without stopping the set**: `[10:14]`, `[20:31]` "you
  can't do it. Go to a lighter weight"; "if you have to drop the weight, drop it as long as you
  don't stop."
sections.heading: Form cues and body signals addressed

sections.body:
- **"The beast" (move)** — a standing side-to-side touch-down-and-twist sequence into a stationary
  sprint, named by Kalev as his favorite move in the session `[26:34]`.
- **"Clio lunge"** — the source's own name (as transcribed) for a continuous alternating lateral
  lunge with a 10-second hold on the forward leg `[22:31]`.
- **In-and-out** — a low, wide squat with lateral stepping in and out, targeted at the inner
  thighs, hips, and glutes `[18:21]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"That's what separates the men from their boy"** `[22:31]` — used at the end of a sumo-squat
  hold to frame the isometric hold as the differentiating part of the move.
- **The 1-to-10 scale itself as a communication tool** `[06:11]`, `[18:21]` — used repeatedly across
  the session as a shorthand for "not hard enough yet," reusable independent of this specific
  workout.
- **"Thank you for the gift you just gave me"** `[30:35]` — reframing a stretch hold as gratitude
  rather than a chore.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational follow-along video, not a studied claim; intensity feedback is
entirely self-reported by the on-camera participants (Nick and Eric) rather than measured:

- **The exertion target is stated as self-assessed, with the instructor pushing the floor up
  rather than measuring it independently**: `[06:11]` the 1–10 scale is Kalev asking the
  participant to name a number, not a heart-rate or other external measurement.
- **Regressions are offered as standing options throughout, not exceptions**: `[05:10]`, `[10:14]`,
  `[17:20]`, `[20:31]`, `[29:35]` — no-bench, lighter-weight, no-jump, and no-partner-equipment
  substitutes are each named in the moment they'd be needed, not held back as advanced-only
  content.
- **Fun and safety are named as co-equal rules to form, not subordinate to intensity**: `[11:14]`
  "Rule number one, stay safe. Rule number two, keep your form. And rule number three, you got to
  have fun with the beast" — stated as a fixed rule set partway through a high-intensity segment.

sections.body:
No other Body Beast cardio-specific session exists yet to compare against. Against `basics`, which
names the Beachbody Jump Mat specifically for this workout ("You will really appreciate this mat
when doing Beast Cardio" — `basics`[05:06]), this session's own transcript never mentions a mat or
jump-impact surface, only a bench for calf raises/toe taps — worth checking against the video
itself (not just its audio) once other Body Beast sessions are notated, since a floor mat could be
visible on screen without being named aloud. Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01], which
draws its safety line at joint/body pain rather than form imperfection, this source's safety framing
is closer to "keep going, adjust load or range, but don't stop" — a difference in where the
stop-signal is set that is worth tracking as more Body Beast sessions are added.

sections.body:
**This DVD is explicitly a compilation, not new workout material — full repeats of Stretch for
Flexibility and Balance and Agility — and its only genuinely new content is a guided walkthrough
of the RUSHFIT Fitness Assessment**, framed as a repeatable progress-tracking tool rather than a
one-time test: `[1:17:21]` "I'm going to explain to you how to use the rush fit assessment in
your own program. The assessment consists of four exercises: squats, push-ups, sit-ups, and
burpees."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
Runs, in order: the Rush Fit Warmup `[00:00]`–`[10:28]`; the full Stretch for Flexibility program
`[11:30]`–`[38:51]` (identical to `stretch-for-flexibility`, down to the same "yin to the yang"
framing and the same clench-and-relax closing sequence); the Rush Fit Warmup again `[38:51]`–
`[50:39]`; and the full Balance and Agility workout `[50:39]`–`[1:17:21]` (identical to
`balance-and-agility`, including the same closing "not good enough for you" perfection-standard
discussion). See those two notes for the full breakdown — nothing here diverges from them in
either content or cueing.
sections.heading: Repeated content (00:00–1:17:21)

sections.body:
Four exercises, 60 seconds each at maximum effort, with a 20-second break between:
**squat → push-up → sit-up → burpee**. This matches the assessment table in the program's Workout
Guide PDF exactly (same four exercises, same GSP reference scores listed there: 75 squats, 57
push-ups, 55 sit-ups, 22 burpees). The stated purpose is comparison over time, not a pass/fail
bar: `[1:17:21]` "You'll find that if you stick with the program... every time you come back and
test you should notice an increase in your performance which associates to an increase in your
overall fitness." Form is explicitly prioritized over raw rep count, with an expected and
acceptable decline as fatigue sets in: `[1:17:21]` "you don't want to do more repetitions at the
cost of form. Naturally as you start to fatigue a little bit of a decrease in form is to be
expected, but if you start to have a complete decay of the movement, you want to rest."

GSP calls the burpee round directly, without irony, the hardest part of the whole assessment:
`[1:24:47]` "That's the worst day of my life... but that's what I need." followed immediately by
a genuine rationale: "we need to enjoy this — the release of pain after the training... that's
what is good."
sections.heading: The RUSHFIT Fitness Assessment (1:17:21–1:24:47)

sections.body:
The same hip flexor, butterfly/straddle, seated hamstring, hip-extensor rotation, quadruped lat,
and kneeling chest/delt stretch sequence as `the-fight-conditioning-workout`'s cool-down, including
the identical closing framing of the cool-down as a mental transition, not just physical recovery:
`[1:33:22]` "For me, I use the cool down as a way to change my mind... to make the transition by
being the fighter to the everyday normal guy."
sections.heading: Cool-down (1:25:50–1:34:22)

sections.body:
- **Expected form decay under fatigue is named explicitly as the assessment's own tolerance
  line**: `[1:17:21]` a "decrease in form is to be expected" but "complete decay of the movement"
  is the point to rest, not push through.
- **First-attempt scores are explicitly reframed as a baseline, not a verdict**: `[1:17:21]`
  "you might find that the numbers aren't exactly what you would hope them to be in comparison to
  George... but you'll find that if you stick with the program... you should notice an increase."

  thought you could do" is named as an expected, normal outcome.
- **Difficulty is acknowledged directly and without spin** for the burpee round specifically:
  `[1:24:47]` "the worst day of my life" — stated as GSP's own genuine in-the-moment reaction, not
  walked back afterward.

sections.body:
**Sagi Kalev names the specific back muscles this session targets before the first set — rhomboids,
traps, lats — and both heads of the biceps, framing the visible goal as a V-taper physique rather
than a generic "back and arms" day.** `[00:00]` "We work in the back, the rhombus, the traps, the
lats. We work in the short part of the biceps, the long part of the biceps... when you're gonna
have that V shape, that V-tape, when you're gonna see your lats sticking out of your shirt, you're
gonna go, Yes, I did it."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
Light jog, arm circles ("a lot of blood going to the shoulder... we're gonna use them a lot in the
workout" `[01:16]`), walk-out-to-plank holds, then three light-weight movement rehearsals that
mirror the session's main lifts: a light deadlift (`[02:16]`, "shoulders back, chest up"), a light
bent-over row (`[02:16]`–`[03:16]`, "keep the weights parallel to the floor"), and a light reverse
fly (`[03:16]`, "glutes out... don't let nothing else move besides raising your elbows up").
sections.heading: Warm-up (01:16–03:16)

sections.body:
Escalating weight across rounds, capped with a drop set. Round one, 15 reps, form cue: `[04:16]`
"bend down. Keep your chest up. Shoulders back. Glutes out... come up. Squeeze your rhombus.
Squeeze your traps." A named principle governs load selection: `[05:17]` "keep your ego outside the
door. Keep your form. If you can't do it, drop the weight." Round two drops to 12 reps at heavier
weight; round three is a drop set — 8 reps at 50 lb with no rest, straight into a lighter-weight set
— stated explicitly: `[06:17]` "Remember drop set. Eight. Drop to eight. No rest."
sections.heading: Set 1 — Deadlift, single set (03:16–08:17)

sections.body:
Dumbbell pull-over on a stability ball (head and neck supported on the ball, weight brought from
overhead down to the chest and back) superset directly with pull-ups, no rest between the two
exercises. Isolation cue on the pull-over: `[09:18]` "trying to isolate the triceps and just the
lat... he's not going too low to take the tension of the shoulders. All lat." A limited-equipment
substitute is repeated at nearly every exercise in this session: `[09:18]`, `[10:18]`, `[12:18]`,
`[17:21]`, `[20:21]`, `[21:22]`, "if you have limited equipment, watch Nick" (dumbbells in place of
a barbell or an EZ bar). Pull-up reps run 10, then 12 at heavier load, then a final 10-rep set,
each paired with a corresponding pull-over set at increasing weight (20s → 40s).
sections.heading: Set 2 — Pull-over / pull-up superset (08:17–15:18)

sections.body:
Three exercises run back-to-back with no rest, repeated for four total rounds at escalating weight
(15 reps down to 8 reps as weight increases). Bent-over EZ-bar row form: `[16:18]` "bend down...
bring the bar right underneath your knees and bring it all the way to the middle of your
midsection." One-arm dumbbell row, braced on a bench: `[17:21]` "my arms on the bench. Keep your
chest up. Extend the other leg out." Seated reverse fly: `[19:21]` "sit on the bench. Feet at 90
degrees. Chest leaning forward. Keep it up straight back and extend your arms up... keep your chin
down," with an explicit isolation check: `[23:27]` "I'm not moving my body. Only my arms coming
up... work on the back of the shoulders, going all the way to the traps and the rhomboids."
sections.heading: Set 3 — Giant set: bent-over EZ-bar row, one-arm row, seated reverse fly (15:18–27:30)

sections.body:
Named directly as Kalev's own favorite move in the session: `[27:30]` "Set number 4. This is my
favorite move." Three 30-second max-effort rounds, form emphasis on elbow path rather than pure
rep count: `[27:30]` "bringing his elbows in. We work in the lower lats. Upper lats. We work in the
whole back," with an explicit pace correction: `[28:31]` "it's about getting a big back. It's not
about speeding up. Stay with the form."
sections.heading: Set 4 — Underhand-grip chin-ups, 30-second rounds (27:30–30:33)

sections.body:
Supinating curl, seated on a stability ball for stability challenge, escalating weight across three
rounds (15 → 12 → 8 reps) with the third round a drop set. Named target framing: `[31:34]` "This is
the gun show. We're going to blast it. We're going to build the biceps all the way." Form cue on
elbow position: `[32:36]` "Elbows down. You don't want to raise them up. This is biceps. Anything
else."
sections.heading: Set 5 — Bicep curl, single set with drop set (30:33–34:38)

sections.body:
A "single, single, double" combo pattern — one rep each arm individually, then one rep both arms
together, counted as a single repetition of the set: `[35:41]` "Single. Single. Double... that was
one rep." The long head of the biceps gets an in-source nickname here: `[35:41]` "this is
everything you work in the long part of the biceps. There you go. We call it the broccoli." Weight
escalates across three rounds (15 → 12 → 8 reps).
sections.heading: Set 6 — Hammer curl, combo set (34:38–40:45)

sections.body:
Standing curl, close/reverse grip, chest up, minimal elbow drift: `[41:45]` "elbows back, tight.
Chest up. Slightly bend your knees and come all the way up without raising your elbows." A
completion-optional safety line is stated directly rather than implied: `[41:45]` "no matter what
weight you use, it's okay if you can't finish the reps." Three rounds, escalating weight, closing
in a drop set (12 → 8 reps).
sections.heading: Set 7 — Close-grip EZ-bar curl, single set into drop set (40:45–46:51)

sections.body:
A back/core finisher done prone on the floor rather than with weights: `[46:51]` "lie flat right
there. You want to keep your chest up. Keep your arms out. And you want to open your hands and
your fingers all the way out... we're opening the chest and we're stretching, squeezing on the
lower back." Nutrition is folded directly into the coaching cue between rounds: `[47:51]` "Stay
with it. Take your supplements. Eat what's on the plan."
sections.heading: Set 8 — Cobra, two 30-second rounds (46:51–48:54)

sections.body:
Standing lat stretch, arm extended overhead, wrist grabbed and pulled into a side bend, breathing
paced explicitly: `[48:54]` "Breathe in. Breathe out." A bench-assisted lat stretch follows, elbow
dropped and hand brought behind the head while leaning into the stretch, with a stated tolerance
rule: `[49:54]` "Stretch it. Feel it. Don't force it. It has to be in the right tolerance." Closes
with a standing shoulder/neck stretch, fingers crossed in front, chin dropped on two paced breaths
`[50:54]`.
sections.heading: Stretch sequence (48:54–50:54)

sections.body:
- **"Keep your ego outside the door" is stated as the governing rule for weight selection**:
  `[05:17]` explicitly framed as more important than hitting a target weight.
- **Rep completion is explicitly not required for safety's sake**: `[41:45]` "it's okay if you
  can't finish the reps."
- **A dedicated limited-equipment substitute is named at nearly every exercise**, not just once:
  `[09:18]`, `[10:18]`, `[12:18]`, `[17:21]`, `[20:21]`, `[21:22]` — dumbbells in place of a
  barbell/EZ bar throughout.
- **Isolation is checked by what does *not* move, not just by what does**: `[09:18]` "trying to
  isolate the triceps and just the lat"; `[23:27]` "I'm not moving my body. Only my arms coming
  up."
- **A stretch's depth is capped by tolerance, not by a fixed count**: `[49:54]` "Don't force it. It
  has to be in the right tolerance."
- **Load is explicitly written down as a tracking discipline**: `[20:21]` "make sure you write the
  weights. That's what I used to do all the time until I got it right" — repeated after nearly
  every set.
sections.heading: Form cues and body signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Giant set** — three (or more) exercises performed back-to-back with no rest between any of
  them, distinct from a superset's two `[15:18]`.
- **Drop set** — finishing a lift's last round at a reduced weight immediately, with no rest,
  stated explicitly each time it's used: `[06:17]` "Remember drop set. Eight. Drop to eight. No
  rest."
- **Combo set** — one repetition defined as single-arm reps on each side followed by a
  simultaneous both-arms rep, demonstrated on the hammer curl as "single, single, double"
  `[35:41]`.
- **"The broccoli"** — the source's own nickname for a fully flexed, peaked long head of the
  biceps `[35:41]`.
- **Dynamic set training** — reused from `basics`[01:01]; this session is the first to actually
  demonstrate its named set types (single, super, giant, drop, combo) in sequence rather than list
  them.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"I'm building a house here... that's a high rise"** `[44:48]` — Kalev's own framing of
  progressively heavier drop-set weight as construction, reusable for any escalating-load segment.
- **"That's the smell of getting huge"** `[36:41]` — muscular pump described in sensory rather than
  purely visual terms.
- **John's origin story as a motivational aside**: `[38:45]` "John was a skinny, skinny boy when he
  was young... he said, I'm going to get bigger... and that's what happened" — used to connect a
  visible physique on screen to a stated multi-year effort, not a quick result.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational training-partner video; its evidence is the coach's technique
narration and two training partners' (John and Nick) visible performance, not citation or
measurement:

- **Safety is stated as a standing rule repeated at nearly every new exercise, not a one-time
  disclaimer**: `[16:18]`, `[41:45]`, `[44:48]` "always, always make sure you got the safety zone";
  "it's okay if you can't finish the reps"; "now I got to keep it safe."
- **Individual load variation is shown, not asserted**: `[05:17]` Kalev, John, and Nick each name
  different personal weights on the same lift (20s/40s/42s) rather than a single prescribed number.
- **Confidence-building is named as a stated side effect, conditioned on time**: `[44:48]` "you can
  lift this weight. You can do anything you want. That's how you build confidence. But you know
  what? It took me a long time to get here."
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
No other Body Beast strength session has been notated yet to compare set structure against.
Against `basics`, which lists "single sets, supersets, drawing sets, progressive sets, drop sets,
force sets, combo sets, and multi sets" as the full roster (`basics`[01:01]), this session
demonstrates only five of those eight named types (single, super, giant, drop, combo) — worth
checking whether "giant set" as used here is the source's synonym for what `basics` calls a
"multi set," since `basics` does not separately define either term, or whether the remaining
named types (drawing, progressive, force) appear in later Body Beast sessions not yet notated.
Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01], whose safety line is drawn at pain rather than
form, this session's safety framing ("it's okay if you can't finish the reps," `[41:45]`) is closer
to a completion-optional standard than a pain-threshold one — a difference worth tracking as more
Body Beast sessions are added.

sections.body:
**Sagi Kalev calls this Body Beast's foundation session and states its target explicitly as the
whole chest — top to bottom — plus all three triceps heads, tying the payoff directly to a
shirtless-beach visual rather than a strength number.** `[00:00]` "This is the foundation of the
workout, the built workout. Working the chest all around from top to bottom, the triceps, all the
three heads of the triceps... when you go on the beach and you're going to take your shirt off,
that's the first thing that people are going to see."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
Jog, then extended-arm shoulder rolls in both directions (`[01:13]`, "elbows stay to the top, both
sides... nothing else is moving. The only thing you're doing is breathing"), into a graduated
close-grip push-up progression: halfway range first (`[02:13]`, "go halfway down... this is not
about going faster. This is about getting warmed up"), then full range at a wider-than-shoulder
stance with a named target: `[03:15]` "focus on the tricep. And make sure you are squeezing your
chest with the bottom of your palm." A knee-drop regression is offered at both stages: `[02:13]`,
`[03:15]` "drop your knees down" / "drop your knees if you can't finish."
sections.heading: Warm-up (01:13–03:15)

sections.body:
Three escalating-weight rounds (15 → 12 → 8 reps), head supported on a stability ball. Form cue:
`[04:16]` "bring the weights to your side of your chest. Focus on your legs. Everything nice and
tight. And press it to the top... squeeze your legs." Round three is a named drop set: `[06:18]`
"drop into eight. Heavyweight. Going to lighter weight. This is our drop set. No rest." Between
sets, Kalev states the reason for writing weights down as a standing rule rather than a one-off
reminder: `[08:18]` "I'm going to keep saying it and say it like a broken record... that's how next
workout you will know where to start."
sections.heading: Set 1 — Flat dumbbell press, single set with drop set (03:15–08:18)

sections.body:
Two exercises with no rest between, escalating together across three rounds (15+15 → 12+12 →
8+8, the last round explicitly a combined drop set and superset). Fly form: `[09:18]` "open your
arm. Keep your chest up. As you come up, pull your chest to the top. Lock on your chest." Press
form, done immediately after with no break: `[10:18]` "Remember, there's no rest on the superset."
Kalev names the muscle-region coverage directly: `[10:18]` "We work in chest. We work in the middle
of the chest. We work in everything. Total package."
sections.heading: Set 2 — Incline fly / incline press superset (09:18–18:18)

sections.body:
Three exercises run back-to-back with no rest, three rounds at escalating weight (15 → 12 → 8
reps). Partial fly is explicitly a half-range move, tension held rather than released at the
midpoint: `[20:18]` "you go in halfway. Open. Go halfway up. Stop right there. You want to keep the
tension right there on the chest the whole time... if you have to drop the weights, that's okay.
As long as you finish." Decline push-up, feet elevated on the bench: `[21:18]` "make sure you are
squeezing... from the bottom of your hand all the way to your lower chest. Keep your glutes up."
Failure is named directly as a training signal rather than something to avoid: `[22:18]` "That was
failure. That's when you really know when your body is working."
sections.heading: Set 3 — Giant set: flat close-grip press, partial fly, decline push-up (18:18–28:19)

sections.body:
Named in-source as "line, plate, triceps... triceps extensions" `[28:19]`, done lying back with
weights lowered to the sides of the head and extended up, elbows held in. Kalev states an explicit
priority order at the top of this set: `[28:19]` "Safety number one. Form number two. And the
number one rule is have fun." A negative/positive terminology distinction is introduced: `[31:19]`
"on the way down, that's your negative. On the way up, that's your positive." Round three is a
drop set, defined again in-source: `[31:19]` "a drop set is when you're going back to back and you
drop the weights without rest... bring your heavier weights to the lighter weights back to back."
A completion-over-count framing recurs here: `[30:19]` "if it was too heavy and you couldn't finish
those reps, you can drop the weight down. But finish. We're all about finish."
sections.heading: Set 4 — Lying dumbbell triceps extension, single set with drop set (28:19–33:19)

sections.body:
Kickback: staggered stance, elbow raised and locked, forearm extended back without dropping the
elbow — `[34:19]` "raise your elbow up. Close to your left. And extend it as high as you can.
Without dropping your elbow" — with the source naming the isolation check directly: `[35:19]` "the
only thing that's moving is your arm going up and down. Focus on the pinky going up." Followed
immediately (no rest, per superset rule restated at `[36:19]`) by close-grip push-ups. Escalates
across three rounds to a combined drop set/superset finish at `[39:19]`–`[41:19]`.
sections.heading: Set 5 — One-arm kickback / close-grip push-up superset (33:19–42:19)

sections.body:
One minute of bench (or chair) dips, with an explicit at-home substitute named up front: `[42:19]`
"you guys don't have a bench at home. You can use a chair. You can use anything that is stable."
Form cue on range and target: `[43:19]` "squeeze right from here. The bottom of your palm going
right to the top of your triceps... it's not about how many you do. It's about doing it right." A
mid-set regression is offered without stopping the clock: `[43:19]` "bring your feet back. Keep it
at 90 degrees right there. And go a shorter move." Immediately followed by one minute of a
reverse-crunch-style ab move (knees rolled to the chest), with a named muscle to avoid substituting
in: `[45:19]` "don't use your hip flexors, which are right here. Go right to the chest... slightly
bend them and roll back up with your chest."
sections.heading: Set 6 — Bench dip and reverse-crunch finisher (42:19–46:19)

sections.body:
Standing torso-rotation chest/shoulder stretch, breath-paced: `[47:19]` "breathe from your nose.
Exhale from your mouth." Overhead triceps stretch, each arm, with an explicit no-force rule:
`[48:19]` "Don't force anything. Just let it be. Feel the stretch." Closes with a standing
shoulder-and-chest stretch: fingers crossed, hands drawn back, chin dropped, shoulders rolled,
paced breathing repeated `[49:19]`.
sections.heading: Stretch and cooldown (46:19–49:19)

sections.body:
- **A completion-over-count rule recurs across multiple sets, not just once**: `[20:18]`, `[30:19]`,
  `[37:19]` "if you have to drop the weights, that's okay. As long as you finish"; "it's not about
  how many you do. It's about how right you do."
- **Failure is explicitly reframed as useful information, not a stopping point to avoid**:
  `[22:18]` "That was failure. That's when you really know when your body is working."
- **A negative/positive vocabulary is introduced for tempo control**: `[31:19]` "on the way down,
  that's your negative. On the way up, that's your positive."
- **Isolation is checked by naming the one thing that should move**: `[35:19]` "the only thing
  that's moving is your arm going up and down."
- **A specific compensating muscle is named and excluded on the ab finisher**: `[45:19]` "don't use
  your hip flexors... go right to the chest."
- **Stretch force is explicitly capped**: `[48:19]` "Don't force anything. Just let it be."
sections.heading: Form cues and body signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Negative / positive (tempo)** — the lowering phase of a lift versus the lifting phase, named
  explicitly as distinct halves of a rep `[31:19]`.
- **Partial fly** — a fly variant stopped at half range, with tension deliberately held rather than
  released at the midpoint `[20:18]`.
- **One-arm kickback** — staggered stance, elbow locked and raised, forearm extended straight back
  to isolate the triceps `[34:19]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"That's how we get big... that's how we get bigger... it's better. What you always wanted."**
  `[14:18]` — Kalev's own escalating-repetition motivational phrasing tied directly to load
  progression.
- **"You know what happens? That was Sean triceps" (smoke/smell running gag)** `[36:19]`, `[47:19]`
  — a recurring bit used to mark a set's visible/felt intensity rather than a literal claim.
- **"Barbie" as a contrast term for insufficient effort**: `[11:18]`, `[44:19]` "this is the beast
  workout. Not the girly workout. You hear that Barbie?" — noted here as the source's own framing,
  not adopted terminology.

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational training-partner video; its evidence is Kalev's technique narration
and two training partners' (Sean and Richard's) visible performance, not citation or measurement:

- **Safety and form are stated as ranked priorities, fun included as a named rule rather than an
  aside**: `[28:19]` "Safety number one. Form number two. And the number one rule is have fun."
- **Individual load and rep variation is shown directly rather than prescribed as one number**:
  `[05:16]`, `[37:19]` Kalev, Sean, and Richard each state different personal weights on the same
  lift (20s/25s/30s; later 8/10 vs. 15/20 on kickbacks).
- **A stretch's depth is explicitly capped by feel, not a fixed hold count**: `[48:19]` "Don't force
  anything. Just let it be. Feel the stretch."

sections.body:
Against `build-back-and-bis`, the sessions share the same set-type vocabulary (single, super,
giant, drop) and the same standing rules — "write the weights down," a completion-optional safety
line, and a limited-equipment training-partner substitute — suggesting these are fixed program-wide
conventions rather than session-specific choices; worth confirming once the remaining `build-`/
`bulk-`/`tempo-` sessions are notated. One difference worth tracking: this session states an
explicit three-part priority order — "safety number one, form number two... have fun" (`[28:19]`)
— where `build-back-and-bis`[05:17] states only "keep your ego outside the door. Keep your form,"
without naming fun as a formal rule; whether that third element is stated in every session or only
some is not yet resolved. Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01], whose safety line sits at
pain rather than form, this session's "as long as you finish" framing is again closer to a
completion standard than a pain threshold.

sections.body:
**Sagi Kalev calls legs his own favorite body part to train and names all four major leg regions
up front — quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves — framing the session's payoff as reversing
underdeveloped ("chicken") legs specifically, not general lower-body fitness.** `[00:00]` "Build
legs, my favorite body parts. We will use single set, super set, giant sets. We're going to work
the caps, the hamstrings, the glutes, the quads, all around it. You know what? It's time to get rid
of your chicken legs."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
High knees, hip circles ("we got to warm up the hips" `[01:04]`), alternating reverse lunges (front
leg held at 90 degrees, chest open), and bodyweight sumo squats, toes turned out — `[01:04]` "you
want to stretch your glutes. You want to work your thighs." Closes with high knees at increased
pace before weights are picked up.
sections.heading: Warm-up (01:04–02:04)

sections.body:
Weight held under the chin, close to the body, three escalating rounds (15 → 12 → 8, the third an
explicit no-rest drop set). Depth and knee tracking are both named: `[02:04]` "go as low as you
can... make sure you don't knock your knees." The drop set is defined again in-source: `[04:04]`
"Remember, there is no rest on a drop set." A recurring effort framing appears here for the first
time in this session: `[05:04]` "get to that zone. Find that place. Failure is not an option."
sections.heading: Set 1 — Sumo squat, single set with drop set (02:04–05:04)

sections.body:
Alternating front lunges superset directly with a bench step-up into a reverse lunge, no rest
between the two moves, escalating weight across rounds (15 → 12 → 8 per leg). Step-up form: `[06:04]`
"straighten your legs out. Ninety degree. Right there on the opposite legs. And pull your shoulders
up as you're extending your chest." An explicit "too easy" exchange is used to frame intensity:
`[09:04]` "Is it pretty easy? ... It's never too easy. You know what? Because you don't build legs
if it's too easy." A stated safety allowance recurs through this set: `[12:05]` "if you have to stop
and drop the weights, that's okay." One line frames the set's difficulty directly rather than
minimizing it: `[14:05]` "Your body saying no. Your heart saying yes."
sections.heading: Set 2 — Front lunge / step-up-to-reverse-lunge superset (05:04–16:05)

sections.body:
Three exercises run back-to-back with no rest, across four escalating rounds (15 → 12 → 8 reps
twice more at increasing weight). Squat cue on knee tracking: `[17:05]` "make sure your knees don't
buckle. Let them face your big toes." Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated on a bench), with
an explicit limited-equipment substitute: `[17:05]` "if you don't have a bench, watch Big Mac right
there." One-leg stiff-leg deadlift, named in-source as "the ski move," with a posture analogy:
`[23:12]` "think about there's a broom going right through you, and it can go forward or
backwards" — used to cue a flat, hinge-only back line. A session-wide rule is stated mid-set:
`[23:12]` "Rule number one, stay safe... you got to have fun. You don't have fun, it's not worth
it." A no-weight regression is offered explicitly for the advanced squat variant: `[14:05]` "if you
have to do it with no weight, you know what? This workout is advanced."
sections.heading: Set 3 — Giant set: squat, Bulgarian split squat, one-leg stiff-leg deadlift (16:05–29:16)

sections.body:
Standing single-leg calf raise, 30 seconds each leg, weight held close to the body: `[30:18]`
"bring your calves all the way. Extend them to the floor as low as you can. But don't touch it. Go
as high as you can." Immediately into seated calf raise, weight balanced on the knee, 30 seconds:
`[31:18]` "the weights are always in control... you want to stretch it. You want to squeeze as high
as you can." Followed by a seated ab move — leaning back, knees rolled to the chest — run for two
30-second rounds: `[33:18]` "you're going to roll your legs. You're going to lean back. And you're
going to bring your knees all the way to your chest." The block closes with a 30-second flat-bench
core roll-out: `[36:19]` "roll it out... it's all about success." Difficulty is acknowledged
directly rather than softened: `[36:19]` "It's not easy. I never said it's going to be easy."
sections.heading: Set 4 — Calves and finisher ab work (29:16–37:19)

sections.body:
Standing hamstring reach, straight leg forward, toes reached for, with a named regression: `[37:19]`
"if you're not flexible, bend that knee. If it's shaking, just hold it." Standing quad stretch,
knee drawn close to the body, explicitly capped by force: `[38:19]` "stretch it whatever you can.
As high as you can. Don't force it." Closes with a two-sided kneeling hip-flexor stretch, hands on
the front knee, leaning back with a paced breath: `[38:19]` "feel the soya's [psoas] right there.
Feel the hip flexors. Take a deep breath."
sections.heading: Stretch and cooldown (37:19–39:19)

sections.body:
- **Knee tracking is named on two separate lifts in this session**: `[17:05]` "let them face your
  big toes" (squat); a similar "don't let your knee go all the way out" cue on the Bulgarian squat
  `[18:07]`.
- **A stop-and-drop safety allowance is repeated across multiple sets**, not stated once:
  `[12:05]`, `[22:10]` "if you have to stop and drop the weights, that's okay"; "if you have to
  drop the weights, that's what you do."
- **"Too easy" is treated as a red flag rather than a compliment**: `[09:04]` "it's never too easy...
  because you don't build legs if it's too easy."
- **A no-weight regression is named explicitly for the giant set's hardest variant**: `[14:05]`
  "if you have to do it with no weight, you know what? This workout is advanced."
- **Calf-raise range is bounded at both ends**: `[30:18]` "extend them to the floor as low as you
  can. But don't touch it. Go as high as you can."
- **Stretch depth is explicitly capped by force, and a shaking limb is a hold-not-push signal**:
  `[37:19]` "if it's shaking, just hold it"; `[38:19]` "don't force it."

sections.body:
- **"The ski move" (one-leg stiff-leg deadlift)** — the source's own name for a single-leg
  stiff-leg deadlift, bar or dumbbell brought close to the working leg with a flat back `[19:07]`.
- **Bulgarian squat** — rear foot elevated on a bench, front leg doing the work, named directly in
  the transcript `[17:05]`.

sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"Think about there's a broom going right through you"** `[23:12]` — a straight-back posture cue
  for hip-hinge movements, reusable for any stiff-leg or deadlift-pattern exercise.
- **"Your body saying no. Your heart saying yes."** `[14:05]` — framing mid-set difficulty as a
  motivational contrast rather than a stop signal.
- **"Success is the only option. Failure is not."** `[15:05]`, `[36:19]` — repeated verbatim across

sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational training-partner video; its evidence is Kalev's technique narration
and two training partners' (Richard and Big E/Edwin's) visible performance, not citation or
measurement:

- **Difficulty is stated directly rather than downplayed**: `[12:05]` "This is brutal... This is
  tough. This is hard."; `[36:19]` "It's not easy. I never said it's going to be easy."
- **A stop-and-drop safety allowance is repeated as standing permission, not a one-time
  exception**: `[12:05]`, `[22:10]`, `[30:18]` — offered at three separate points across three
  different exercises.
- **Individual load variation is shown directly**: `[13:05]`, `[21:09]` Richard and Kalev state
  different personal starting/ending weights on the same lifts (15→30, 20→40) rather than one
  prescribed number.
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
Against `build-back-and-bis`[05:17] and `build-chest-and-tris`[28:19], both of which state a
priority-order rule (ego/form, or safety/form/fun) once near the start of a set, this session
states a similar three-part rule ("stay safe... you got to have fun," `[23:12]`) mid-session rather
than at the top — consistent with these being fixed program-wide conventions restated at different
points rather than session-specific. The "success only, failure is not an option" framing at
`[05:04]`/`[15:05]`/`[36:19]` sits in tension with `build-chest-and-tris`[22:18], which reframes
hitting failure as useful information ("That was failure. That's when you really know when your
body is working") rather than something to avoid outright — worth resolving once more sessions are
notated whether "failure" means muscular failure (embraced) or giving up (rejected) in each case,
since this transcript's wording doesn't disambiguate. Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01],
whose safety line is pain rather than form, this session's repeated "stop and drop the weight" offer
is again closer to a completion/load-adjustment standard than a pain threshold.

**Sagi Kalev calls shoulders the single most visually impressive body part to train, and states the
mechanism directly: rounding all three deltoid heads visually narrows the waist by contrast, an
effect he names before any lift is shown.** `[00:00]` "Build shoulders. The most impressive body
part on your physique. You have big shoulders, you're gonna have small waist... think about round
shoulders like two balloons with small waist. And that's what build shoulders is all about."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
Light jog, then extended-arm circles both directions (`[01:09]`, "keep your chest open. Keep your
legs and your glutes tight"), followed by light-weight rehearsals of the session's main lifts:
front raise to a V shape (`[02:09]`, "use very light weights. This is just to warm up the
shoulders. Nothing else"), lateral raise (`[02:09]`), shoulder press (`[03:09]`), upright row
(`[03:09]`), and reverse fly (`[03:09]`–`[04:09]`, "working the back of the shoulders... if you
start getting heavy, drop the weights. This is just to warm up").
sections.heading: Warm-up (01:09–04:09)

sections.body:
Three escalating rounds (15 → 12 → 8, the third a no-rest drop set), on a stability ball. Tempo is
named explicitly rather than left implicit: `[05:10]` "going slow down. And explode up." A
limited-equipment note broadens beyond weight substitution here — the ball itself is named as
adding difficulty: `[05:10]` "just because it's the ball doesn't mean it's easy."
sections.heading: Set 1 — Seated shoulder press, single set with drop set (04:09–08:11)

sections.body:
The session's standing rule is stated in full for the first time here: `[09:12]` "Everything has to
be safe. You got to keep your form. And then most of all, you got to have fun with it as you get
huge." Lateral raise form: `[09:12]` "chest up. Shoulders back. Raise it to the side. And make sure
your elbow is slightly bent as you drag the weight from the floor up." Close-grip EZ-bar upright
row, superset directly after with no rest: `[09:12]` "raise your elbows as high as you can. Close
your chin." Wrist position is checked specifically on the lateral raise: `[10:12]` "don't bend your
wrist. Right there with me. Front and back." Three escalating rounds close in a combined drop
set/superset at `[14:15]`–`[15:15]`.
sections.heading: Set 2 — Side lateral raise / upright row superset (08:11–16:15)

sections.body:
Three exercises run back-to-back with no rest, four rounds at escalating weight (15 → 12 → 12 → 8
reps). Reverse-grip press form: `[16:15]` "bring the bar underneath your chin. Press it right to
the top. Lock on your shoulders." Front-raise combo, seated for stability, single-arm reps alternated
then a combined rep counted as one: `[16:15]` "single front raise, single combo, and together. That
one count is one." An added-difficulty note is repeated from Set 1: `[18:20]` "if you don't have a
bench... it's a little bit harder like that because you have to stabilize your body... you have to
use more core." Rear-delt raise closes the giant set, with a named target and a form correction:
`[19:20]` "the back of your shoulders... that small muscle right here. You don't want to cheat. You
want to keep your back straight."
sections.heading: Set 3 — Giant set: reverse-grip press, front-raise combo, rear-delt raise (16:15–24:22)

sections.body:
Standing shrug, chin dropped, traps squeezed at the top: `[26:22]` "raise your shoulders as high as
you can. Squeeze the traps." Superset directly with a bench-supported incline shrug, chest braced
on the raised end of the bench: `[26:22]` "the arms are not doing anything besides raising your
traps all the way up." An isolation check is stated explicitly: `[27:23]` "my arms are not bending.
They're just holding the weight. I'm focusing on the top of my muscles." Named directly as a slow,
controlled ("oscillating") movement rather than a fast one: `[28:28]` "this is an oscillating move.
Right there, you oscillate the traps." Three rounds escalate to a drop set (`[29:29]`–`[31:33]`),
with a form note on standing back up from the heaviest weight: `[30:30]` "make sure you bend your
knees when you stand up. Don't lean with your back."
sections.heading: Set 4 — Trap shrug / incline shrug ("scap traps") superset (25:22–32:34)

sections.body:
Named directly as Kalev's own favorite move in the session: `[32:34]` "we got my favorite move now...
this is the move when I can't sleep at night. That's what I do. I think about how to torture the
beast." A light-weight lateral raise run in a fixed sequence — side, then front, pulled to the top,
back to center — with each full cycle counted as one rep: `[32:34]` "to the side, to the front. Pull
it to the top. Bring it right to the front, to the side, back to the starting point... we got 12
reps. Each one is count as one." A no-weight continuation is offered explicitly rather than
stopping the set at fatigue: `[33:34]` "if you don't finish, there's not another way. You're going
to keep going. Failure is not an option. You drop the weights. You keep going. You're squeezing the
shoulders." Immediately paired with a lying ab finisher — knees rolled to the chest, then a
hip-raise variant with glutes lifted off the bench — for two rounds (15 then 8 reps): `[34:34]`
"roll your knees all the way in to your chest"; `[37:37]` "raise the glutes off the bench... control
it."
sections.heading: Set 5 — "The Giz move" and ab finisher (32:34–38:37)

sections.body:
A brief standing shoulder/lat stretch to each side, followed by fingers crossed overhead with paced
breathing, then arms brought behind the head: `[38:37]` "stretch your lats. Stretch your shoulders...
Cross your fingers. Raise them to the top. Breathe."
sections.heading: Stretch and cooldown (38:37)

sections.body:
The workout itself ends at `[38:37]` ("That was Bill['s] shoulder[s], guys... Thank you. See you
next time"). Everything from `[39:37]` to the end of the file is unrelated Beachbody promotional
content — a P90X advertisement followed by a "Team Beachbody Coach" recruitment reel — not Body
Beast programming, not delivered by Sagi Kalev, and not reflected in this note's exercises or
training-focus facets. It is flagged here rather than silently excluded so the source file's actual
contents stay traceable.

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational training-partner video; its evidence is Kalev's technique narration
and two training partners' (Chris and Big E/Edwin's) visible performance, not citation or
measurement:

- **"Know your limit" is stated as an explicit qualifier on effort, not just encouragement to push
  harder**: `[36:36]` "I know what's about to happen. So I want to stay smart. It's not about being
  right, but being smart. You got to know your limit." This sits alongside, and slightly
  complicates, the same session's "failure is not an option" framing at `[33:34]` — both are
  presented by the same speaker within about two minutes of each other.
- **A stated history is given as the reason for a specific safety caution**: `[11:13]` "I've seen a
  lot in the past. What happened when you don't use the safety" — referenced but not detailed
  further in this transcript.
- **Individual load variation is shown directly**: `[07:11]`, `[23:22]` Kalev, Chris, and Edwin each
  state different personal weights on the same lifts rather than one prescribed number.
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
The safety/form/fun rule at `[09:12]` matches `build-legs`[23:12] and `build-chest-and-tris`[28:19]
closely enough in wording to confirm it as a fixed program-wide rule restated per session rather
than session-specific phrasing. This session is the first to qualify the program's otherwise
consistent "failure is not an option" / "whatever it takes" framing (seen in `build-legs`[05:04]
and `build-back-and-bis`) with an explicit "know your limit" caveat (`[36:36]`) — worth checking
whether later Body Beast sessions restate this qualifier or whether it is unique to this one.
Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01], whose safety line sits at pain rather than form,
this session's closest equivalent is the ball/bench "harder, not easier" framing (`[05:10]`,
`[18:20]`) plus the "know your limit" caveat — a difference in vocabulary but a similar underlying
concern with the same category of risk.

session's ambition ("cannons") from ordinary arm training ("guns") before the first set.**
`[00:00]` "Bulk Arms. The place where it really counts. You want to have big triceps? You want to

sections.body:
Arm circles both directions, then light-weight rehearsals of the session's exercise families:
straight curls (`[01:10]`, "should be lightweight... keep your chest up"), a wider-grip curl
(`[02:10]`), hammer curls — explicitly named as covering both biceps heads: `[02:10]` "working all
sides of the biceps. The long part. The short part" — and a light two-arm overhead triceps
extension (`[02:10]`–`[03:10]`, "hips back, and your chest up"). Closes with high knees before the

sections.body:
The first in-session definition of a progressive set: three weights run back-to-back with no rest,
reps dropping as weight rises. `[04:10]` "I'm starting with a 10. Straight curls... then I'm moving
right away. Going down with the reps. To 20s. With no rest. 12 reps. And then I'm moving again. To
30s. I'm going to do 8 reps. With no rest. You got it guys. That is progressive set." A second round
reverses the direction — heavy to medium to light — named directly as the same technique run
backward: `[06:10]` "we're going to start with the heaviest weight... and then we're going to the
lighter one... we are progressing up, progressing down."
sections.heading: Set 1 — Curl, progressive set (03:10–08:10)

sections.body:
Seated, weight lowered behind the head and pressed up, elbows fixed: `[08:10]` "nothing's moving.
Beside my arms going up and down. Make sure you keep your elbows in." Three escalating rounds
(12 → 8, closing in a drop set), with an effort framing distinct from the program's usual "failure
is not an option": `[10:10]` "success is my only option."
sections.heading: Set 2 — Overhead triceps extension, single set with drop set (08:10–12:10)

sections.body:
Named directly as Kalev's own favorite move in this session, and the first in-session definition of
a force set: `[12:10]` "This is my favorite move in this workout. We got five sets of five reps.
Back. Focusing on the negative. In this move, there's not going up or down with the weight. We're
staying with it." The structure, restated for clarity: `[13:10]` "we got five reps like that. We
don't drop the weights. We hold it for a few. And then we do five more. We got five times to do
that. No breaking down. No dropping. No going up." Emphasis throughout is on the slow eccentric
(lowering) phase rather than the lift itself: `[14:10]` "control it on the way down. Real slow. Let
your muscle fill in it. Squeeze on it. Stretch it."
sections.heading: Set 3 — EZ-bar curl, force set (12:10–16:10)

sections.body:
Named in-source as "crush[ers]": `[16:10]` "this is called crush[ed]... bring the weight lying
down. Extend it up. Lock your elbows in... your hand's going right to your forehead." An isolation
check follows directly: `[17:10]` "make sure your elbows are not [tucked too] tight. They're not
going anywhere besides squeezing your chest. You want to squeeze the chest with your elbows.
That's why you're not working chest. You're only working the triceps." Three escalating rounds
(15 → 12 → 8+8 drop set).
sections.heading: Set 4 — Lying triceps extension ("crush"), single set with drop set (16:10–21:10)

sections.body:
One arm at a time, elbow braced against the top of the knee: `[22:10]` "next to your top of your
knee. And bring your arm all the way up. Without raising your elbow off your knee." Each arm runs
its own full light-medium-heavy progression (15 → 12 → 8) before switching sides, with no rest at
any transition — weight change or side change.
sections.heading: Set 5 — Concentrated hammer curl, progressive set (21:10–27:12)

sections.body:
Staggered stance, elbow raised and fixed, isolation cued through the small finger rather than the
whole hand: `[28:12]`, `[29:12]` "starting with elbow up. Kick back. Extend... focus on the pinky.
As you get up." Each arm again runs its own light-medium-heavy progression (15 → 12 → 8) with no
rest between weights or sides.
sections.heading: Set 6 — Triceps kickback, progressive set (28:12–33:12)

sections.body:
A single 30-rep set, weight plate held behind the head: `[34:12]` "come as high as you can and
squeeze your abs." Nutrition is folded directly into the coaching cue: `[34:12]` "you got to eat
right. Abs, ma[de] in the kitchen, but they're also made on your workout."
sections.heading: Ab finisher — weighted-plate crunch ("old school abs") (34:12–35:13)

sections.body:
Standing side-bend with arms crossed and raised, in-and-out arm extension, then a forward-reaching
chest stretch with a no-force rule stated directly: `[35:13]`–`[36:13]` "don't force it. You just
want to extend this." Closes with a from-the-back triceps/shoulder stretch, breath-paced.
sections.heading: Stretch and cooldown (35:13–36:13)

sections.body:
The workout itself ends at `[36:13]` ("that was amazing. Bulk arms... see you next time"). Everything
from `[37:13]` to the end of the file is unrelated Beachbody promotional content — P90X2, Shakeology,
and P90X advertisements — not Body Beast programming, not delivered as part of the Kalev-led
session, and not reflected in this note's exercises or training-focus facets.
sections.heading: Content note: appended promotional material (37:13–end)

sections.body:
- **Isolation is checked by naming which joint should stay fixed**: `[09:10]`, `[22:10]` "nothing's
  moving besides my arms"; "without raising your elbow off your knee."
- **A specific compensating muscle is named and excluded**: `[17:10]` "you want to squeeze the chest
  with your elbows. That's why you're not working chest. You're only working the triceps" — a
  correction against elbow flare that would recruit the chest instead of the triceps.
- **The eccentric (lowering) phase is called out as the trained variable in the force set**:
  `[14:10]` "control it on the way down. Real slow. Let your muscle fill in it."
- **A load-adjustment safety allowance recurs across sets**: `[08:10]`, `[21:10]` "you have to drop
  the weights. Drop the weights. Just like that... just write it down."
- **A specific isolation checkpoint (the small finger) is used on the kickback**: `[29:12]` "focus
  on the pinky. Extend your triceps."
sections.heading: Form cues and body signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Progressive set** — three weights (light, medium, heavy) run back-to-back with no rest, reps
  decreasing as weight rises; can also run in reverse (heavy to light). First defined in-session
  here, matching the term named without definition in `basics`[01:01] `[04:10]`.
- **Force set** — five sets of five reps at one fixed weight, held rather than dropped between
  sets, with emphasis on a slow negative (lowering) phase rather than a full up/down rep cycle.
  First defined in-session here, matching the term named without definition in `basics`[01:01]
  `[12:10]`.
- **"Crush" (lying triceps extension)** — the source's own shorthand name for a lying triceps
  extension to the forehead `[16:10]`.
- **"Cannons" vs. "guns"** — the source's own escalated term for well-developed arms, used to
  distinguish this session's ambition from ordinary arm training `[00:00]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"That's back in the days when you're still going to kindergarten. Now you're in the next
  phase."** `[10:10]` — used to frame an upcoming drop set as a step up in difficulty from what
  came before.
- **"You train them right. You be nice. Be polite. They'll love you forever."** `[13:10]` — said
  about equipment (a cleaned bar), reused humorously to reinforce the "clean your equipment"
  safety habit.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
An instructional/motivational training-partner video; its evidence is Kalev's technique narration
and two training partners' (John and Nick's) visible performance, not citation or measurement:

- **"Success is my only option" is offered as this session's specific reframing** of the program's
  more common "failure is not an option" phrasing (`[10:10]`; compare `build-legs`[05:04]) — the
  same underlying stance stated in different words rather than a different standard.
- **A completion-optional, load-adjustable safety line recurs at multiple points**: `[08:10]` and
  `[21:10]`,
  `[21:10]` "if you have to drop the weights, you know what? Drop the weights. No problem."
- **Long-term effort is named directly rather than implied**: `[19:10]` "these guys have been
  doing it for a long time. They really, really work hard to get these cannons."
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
This session gives the first in-source definitions of "progressive set" and "force set," two of
the eight set types `basics`[01:01] names without defining — worth checking as more sessions are
notated whether the remaining undefined types ("drawing sets," "combo sets," "multi sets") get
defined elsewhere, and whether `build-back-and-bis`'s "giant set" is one of `basics`'s named types
under a different label (flagged as an open question in `build-back-and-bis`'s own Conflicts
section). The "success is my only option" framing here is a close variant of `build-legs`[05:04]'s
"success is the only option. Failure is not" (restated at `build-legs`[15:05]) — consistent phrasing
across sessions rather than a contradiction. Against RUSHFIT's `balance-and-agility`[37:01], whose safety line
sits at pain rather than form, this session's repeated "drop the weight, just write it down" offer
is again closer to a completion/load-adjustment standard.
